title: And they were all musicals!! #broadway #musicaltheatre #jessiemueller...
transcript: Can you think of a Broadway star with a run of back to back gigs as impressive as the one Jesse Mueller had in the early 2010s? Because welcome to another episode of Overthinking Theatre Throwback where I do retrospectives on recent theatre history. Now, a lot of people might not remember this, but the show that really put Jesse Mueller on the map in New York theatre was not Beautiful, not Waitress, but this very short-lived and pretty poorly-regarded revival of On A Clear Day You Can See Forever opposite Harry Connick Jr. Now, I didn't see this production personally, but I remember when it was playing, the word of mouth was like, “this is bad” “Harry Connick Jr. Is bad” “But what the hell?!” “who is this Jesse Mueler girl? She's amazing!” Mind you, she had been a Chicago actor for a while, but New York audiences had no idea who she was. But they quickly snatched her up She even got a Tony nomination for this, even though the production had long since closed and was otherwise completely shut out But that's when she started what I consider to be one of the most impressively concentrated runs of gigs in recent memory. Just two months after On a Clear Day closed, it was announced that she would be playing Cinderella in the Central Park production of Into the Woods that summer. And only seven weeks after into the Woods closed, she started performances in The Mystery of Edwin Drood on Broadway. *During* that run, she took a break to star in the New York Philharmonic concert version of Carousel as Carrie. And only three weeks after Drood closed, she replaced Kelli O'hara in Nice Work If You Can Get It. That was probably the most crazy concentration of gigs, but still, it was only three months later that she started performances as Carol King in Beautiful in the San Francisco try out That transferred almost immediately to Broadway with only about one month in between runs. And I imagine most of that was spent rehearsing anyway. And speaking of all of the time gaps I've mentioned in this video so far didn't even count rehearsal. About five months after her very successful Tony-winning run in Beautiful, she went to do the out of town tryout of Waitress in Boston that transferred to Broadway six months later and she was in it for about a year. Then she took a crazy long break of 11 months before returning to Broadway and returning to Carousel, this time as Julie Jordan. She was truly booked and blessed there for a long time, and it was very cool to watch this happen in real time, which is why it sticks in my brain so much. But who are some other Broadway actors who had really intensely concentrated back to back runs?
